title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
summary: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible.
